reasoning_traces.think:
The G7 circuit breaker is a sequential calibration drift detector operating on real settled outcomes. It compares the mean calibration error (MCE) over the last 30 bets (fast window) to the MCE over the last 250 bets (slow baseline). When the difference exceeds a threshold of 0.02, it triggers a HALT verdict, blocking all picks from that family. This operator is distinct from the founder's pause list because it is machine-owned, does not overwrite the founder's decisions, and applies even when the founder's opt-in is off. Its failure mode is type I error (false halts), which we empirically bound at zero false halts in 400 perfectly calibrated families. The three-hop wiring ensures that this verdict propagates from the data producer through persistence to the runtime consumer, creating a closed-loop system that prevents drifting families from contributing to downstream predictions.
